security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives where Markdown code fences were mistaken for Ruby backtick execution. The only confirmed issue is an unquoted command substitution in the worktree check, which can mishandle unusual branch names. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Unquoted command substitution in the worktree check
remediation.suggestion: Quote the branch name and use fixed-string matching, such as grep -F -- "$(git branch --show-current)".

remediation.issue: Placeholder shell commands depend on safe manual substitution
remediation.suggestion: Tell users and agents to quote branch names, titles, and paths before running any documented command.

content.value_statement: Finishing a completed branch often leaves teams choosing between merge, pull request, preservation, or discard. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured finish workflow with tests, confirmations, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Checks that the project test suite passes before completion decisions.
Identifies a likely base branch with git merge-base.
Presents four finish options: local merge, pull request, keep branch, or discard.
Guides pull request creation with a summary and test plan.
Requires typed confirmation before destructive discard steps.
Handles worktree cleanup rules for merge, PR, keep, and discard flows.
limitations: It assumes the user or agent knows the correct project test command.
It does not resolve merge conflicts or failing tests by itself.
It depends on local git and optional GitHub CLI availability.
It uses placeholder commands that must be adapted before execution.

use_cases.title: End a feature branch
use_cases.description: Choose whether to merge locally, open a pull request, keep work, or discard it after tests pass.

use_cases.title: Prepare review work
use_cases.description: Create a focused pull request with a concise summary and test plan after implementation is complete.

use_cases.title: Clean temporary worktrees
use_cases.description: Remove finished worktrees only when the selected branch outcome makes cleanup appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Finish My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to finish my current development branch. Verify tests first, then show the four completion options.

prompt_templates.title: Create Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: My implementation is complete. Help me push the branch and create a pull request with a summary and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Merge With Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Finish this branch by checking tests, identifying the base branch, merging locally if I approve, and testing the merged result.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Completion Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my completed branch state, explain the safest finish option, and handle worktree cleanup only after the selected action.

output_examples.input: Implementation is complete and tests pass. Help me finish this branch.
output_examples.output: The skill verifies tests, identifies the base branch, and offers four choices: merge, pull request, keep branch, or discard.

output_examples.input: I want to discard this branch.
output_examples.output: The skill lists what will be deleted and requires the exact typed confirmation before any destructive cleanup.

output_examples.input: Create a pull request for this finished work.
output_examples.output: The skill guides branch push, pull request creation, a concise change summary, and a test plan.

best_practices: Run the project test suite before asking for a finish decision.
Confirm the base branch before merging or opening a pull request.
Use the discard option only after reviewing commits and worktree paths.
anti_patterns: Do not merge or create a pull request while tests are failing.
Do not delete branches or worktrees without exact confirmation.
Do not force-push unless the user explicitly requests it.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to run the project test suite before offering finish options.

faq.question: Can it create a GitHub pull request?
faq.answer: Yes, when the GitHub CLI is available and the user chooses the pull request option.

faq.question: Will it delete my branch without asking?
faq.answer: No. The discard path requires exact typed confirmation before deletion steps.

faq.question: Does it handle merge conflicts?
faq.answer: It can identify the merge workflow, but conflict resolution remains a separate coding task.

faq.question: Can it preserve the worktree?
faq.answer: Yes. The keep option leaves the branch and worktree in place for later action.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
